design_rationale: This was an explicitly randomized parallel-group trial using a computer-generated allocation sequence with 1:1 assignment to magnesium sulphate or placebo.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated with variable blocks and stratification, implemented by an independent third party through a web-based system linked to pre-packed study medication, and baseline characteristics were broadly balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomisation was performed by a computer-generated random allocation sequence in variable blocks of two, four and six... The randomisation process was carried out by a third party (DEFACTUM, Central Region Denmark).

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, caregivers, coordinators, and investigators were blinded with an identical placebo; adherence was high, deviations were not materially imbalanced, and the primary analysis followed intention-to-treat, including the two participants unblinded for serious adverse effects.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The participants, caregivers, and study coordinators at all sites, as well as the investigators were blinded to treatment assignment until all data were collected, the data analyses completed, and the tables and figures were made.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary cerebral-palsy status was ascertained through medical records for all surviving children, deaths were recorded, and all 680 randomized fetuses/children were included in the primary analysis, making outcome missingness negligible.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 321 (100%) were followed-up through medical records... 313 (100%) were followed-up through medical records.

domain_judgments.rationale: Moderate-to-severe cerebral palsy was defined using the established GMFCS, assessed consistently through clinical records and corroborated with a validated questionnaire, while blinding of investigators minimized differential assessment by assigned intervention.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was moderate to severe CP defined as a Gross Motor Function Classification System (GMFCS) of level II to V.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered and states that analyses were planned in advance, but the supplied report does not provide enough protocol or statistical-analysis-plan detail to exclude selective choice among eligible adjusted analyses, and additional secondary outcomes were added after trial initiation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After the initiation of the trial, but prior to unblinding, we added further secondary outcomes for the completeness of the data report.

overall_summary: The trial had robust randomization and concealment, effective blinding, intention-to-treat analysis, essentially complete primary-outcome ascertainment, and appropriate outcome measurement. Some concerns remain about selective reporting because the available text does not fully establish that all eligible outcome analyses were prespecified, and secondary outcomes were added after trial initiation.

design_rationale: The study explicitly used a computer-generated allocation sequence with central telephone randomization to assign women to magnesium sulphate or placebo.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated, stratified, and concealed through central telephone randomization until assignment, with baseline characteristics largely balanced apart from a plausible chance imbalance in PPROM.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomisation numbers were generated by computer using variable block size from 2 to 16 depending on expected recruitment. Central telephone randomisation was managed by staff of the NICU at the Antoine-Be´cle`re Hospital, Clamart, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants were blinded with identical solutions, care otherwise followed standard practice, treatment nonreceipt was similar between groups, and the analysis followed intention to treat despite clinicians being unblinded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The two solutions looked identical so that the women were unaware of whether they received a MgSO4 or placebo solution... All statistical analyses were undertaken on an intention-to-treat basis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Mortality and combined-outcome data were available for all 688 analyzed infants, while ultrasound data were unavailable only for 23 infants who died too early and death was incorporated into the combined primary endpoint.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Outcome data were obtained until hospital discharge for all 564 women and 688 infants... Among the 688 fetuses alive at randomisation, 23 (3.3%) infants never had CUS because they died too early.

domain_judgments.rationale: Mortality was objective, and cranial ultrasound was scheduled and defined consistently across groups, interpreted by blinded senior clinicians, with a blinded central validation substudy showing substantial agreement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: For all surviving infants, CUS was conducted by a senior neonatologist or radiologist in each centre separately and in a blind manner relative to treatment allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcomes and analytic approach were described and trial registration was reported, but no prospectively accessible protocol or statistical analysis plan is provided to rule out selection among adjusted analyses or outcome specifications.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcomes were overall neonatal mortality before hospital discharge, detection of neonatal CUS abnormalities evocative of severe WMI... and the combination of severe WMI, and/or neonatal mortality.

overall_summary: The trial had robust randomization and concealment, largely complete outcome data, intention-to-treat analysis, and blinded outcome assessment. Overall risk is some concerns because the report does not provide a prospectively accessible protocol or statistical analysis plan sufficient to exclude selective reporting among eligible analyses.

design_rationale: Eligible pregnant individuals were explicitly randomly assigned to magnesium sulfate or placebo using a central telephone randomization service with a balanced variable-block schedule.

domain_judgments.rationale: The central variable-block randomization schedule was generated by an investigator outside clinical care, treatment packs were linked to study numbers, and reported baseline characteristics were similar, supporting adequate sequence generation and allocation concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Eligible pregnant individuals were randomly assigned to the magnesium group or the placebo group using a central telephone randomization service... The randomization schedule used balanced, variable block sizes and was performed by an investigator not involved in clinical care.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and trial personnel were blinded, approximately 95% in each group received allocated treatment, and prespecified intention-to-treat analyses were used, making material bias from deviations unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants, staff, investigators, and assessors of the children were blinded to the treatment allocation... Almost 95% of participants in each group received the allocated treatment... [analyses] were conducted following a prespecified statistical analysis plan with an intention-to-treat approach.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only about 81% of randomized offspring contributed to the pediatrician-based primary analysis, although missingness was balanced, investigators found no concerning patterns, and a sensitivity analysis using all sources included about 96% with similar findings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Ofthe infants alive at trial entry, 691 of858 (80.5%) in the magnesium group and 674 of 821 (82.1%) in the placebo group were included for the primary outcome... The sensitivity analysis... included 823 children (95.9%) in the magnesium group and 785 children (95.6%) in the placebo group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Death and cerebral palsy were defined using appropriate standardized criteria, assessed consistently by pediatricians, and child assessors were blinded to allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was death... or cerebral palsy (defined as loss of motor function and abnormalities of muscle tone and power assessed by a pediatrician)... Participants, staff, investigators, and assessors of the children were blinded to the treatment allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome, analysis approach, covariate adjustment, and sensitivity analysis were prespecified in a registered trial protocol and statistical analysis plan, with exploratory multiplicity for secondary outcomes transparently acknowledged.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The trial protocol appears in Supplement 1... The unadjusted and adjusted analyses... were conducted following a prespecified statistical analysis plan... No adjustment was made for multiple comparisons; thus, findings for the secondary outcomes should be interpreted as exploratory.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns, driven by the exclusion of roughly 19% of randomized offspring from the pediatrician-based primary complete-case analysis. Concerns are mitigated by balanced follow-up, blinded assessment, reported evaluation of missingness, and a concordant sensitivity analysis covering approximately 96% of children.

design_rationale: This was an explicitly randomized, placebo-controlled trial using a computer-generated allocation sequence with variable block sizes and masked treatment packs.

domain_judgments.rationale: The computer-generated sequence used variable block sizes, was managed centrally by nonclinical staff, and was implemented through sequential masked treatment packs, with no important baseline imbalance suggesting randomization failure.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study randomization numbers were generated by computer with variable block sizes of 4, 6, or 8 and managed by nonclinical staff at the University of Adelaide’s Maternal Perinatal Clinical Trials Unit. Each study number was placed on a masked treatment pack.

domain_judgments.rationale: Identical placebo packs and blinding of perinatal staff limited intervention-related deviations, crossover was rare, and analyses followed intention-to-treat despite some incomplete infusions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All perinatal staff were blinded to treatment group allocation... All statistical analyses were undertaken on an intention-to-treat basis, including outcome data from women who did not give birth preterm.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome ascertainment was essentially complete, with hospital-discharge data for all randomized women and infants and two-year outcomes for 99% of survivors; only 14 children lacked cerebral-palsy assessment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Outcome data were obtained, up to the time of hospital discharge, on all 1062 women and their 1255 infants alive at the time of randomization, and 2-year corrected age outcomes were available for 1047 children (99% of 2-year survivors).

domain_judgments.rationale: Two-year assessors and the mortality committee were blinded and outcomes were measured similarly across groups, but cerebral-palsy diagnosis depended on individual pediatricians without standardized training, creating some potential measurement variability.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Apart from providing criteria for the diagnosis of cerebral palsy, we did not attempt to train assessors at all 16 centers in its diagnosis. Instead we relied on the judgment of individual developmental pediatricians.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary outcomes and statistical methods were explicitly described, but no prospective registration or publicly available analysis plan is reported, while numerous secondary outcomes and analyses leave some possibility of selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcomes were total pediatric mortality up to a corrected age of 2 years... cerebral palsy at a corrected age of 2 years, and the combined adverse outcome of death or cerebral palsy at 2-year follow-up.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. Randomization, concealment, blinding, intention-to-treat analysis, and follow-up were strong, but nonstandardized cerebral-palsy assessment across centers and the absence of reported prospective registration or a prespecified analysis plan prevent a low-risk judgment.

design_rationale: The study explicitly reports computerized random allocation in stratified blocks of six after women were assigned clinically to one of two parallel trial tracks.

domain_judgments.rationale: A computerized, stratified block-randomization process was used and reported baseline stratification variables were balanced, but the paper does not describe allocation concealment or who could access the sequence before assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: To ensure balance in the randomization process, a computerized program...was used. Consenting women were randomized in stratified blocks of 6 on the basis of race...and gestational age.

domain_judgments.rationale: The preventive trial was doubly masked and intention-to-treat analyses were reported, but the tocolytic comparison was apparently unmasked and control therapy was selected by the attending obstetrician; adherence, crossover, and other deviations are not fully reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In the tocolytic arms, the women were randomized to treatment with either (1) MgSO4...or (2) other tocolytic therapy, according to the attending obstetrician’s choice... In the doubly masked ‘preventive’ arms, women were randomized...

domain_judgments.rationale: Although neonatal outcomes and deaths appear available for the randomized cohort, cerebral-palsy ascertainment depended on survival and 18-month follow-up with no accounting of losses, and the highlighted cord-magnesium analysis included only 82 of 165 infants without evidence that this large missing fraction was unbiased.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of 165 infants, 82 infants have both umbilical cord serum ionized magnesium levels and health outcome data available for analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome definitions and assessment schedules were appropriate, MRI confirmation was used for PVL, and the developmental pediatrician was masked, but masking of the radiologists assessing cranial ultrasound and of death adjudication is not reported; moreover, ascertainment of cerebral palsy only among survivors creates a composite with structurally differing ascertainment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Final ultrasound diagnoses...were made by consensus decisions of 2 pediatric radiologists... The developmentalist was masked to the antenatal exposure variables.

domain_judgments.rationale: No prospective registration or prespecified analysis plan is reported, and the paper presents multiple trial-specific and pooled comparisons, a composite defined as numbers of events rather than participants, both one- and two-sided tests, and several post-randomization exposure/dose analyses, creating substantial scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: These composite comparisons...approached statistical significance (odds ratio, 2.0; 95% CI, 0.99-4.1; 1-sided Fisher exact test, P = .04; 2-sided Fisher exact test, P = .07).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by extensive missing data for the emphasized cord-magnesium analysis and substantial selective-reporting concerns from multiple pooled, composite, one-sided/two-sided, and post-randomization exposure analyses without a reported prespecified plan. Unreported allocation concealment and incomplete masking/deviation information add further concerns.

design_rationale: This was an explicitly randomized controlled trial in which eligible women were assigned using a computer-generated random sequence to magnesium sulfate or matching placebo.

domain_judgments.rationale: The sequence was computer-generated and baseline characteristics were balanced, but the report does not explicitly describe the mechanism used to conceal the allocation sequence until assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Group assignment was made according to a computer-generated random sequence, with stratification according to clinical center and, in twin pregnancies, weeks of gestation (<28 or ≥28).

domain_judgments.rationale: The double-blind, matching-placebo design minimized performance bias, adherence was high with infrequent off-protocol magnesium use, and all participants were analyzed according to randomized assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The data from all patients were analyzed according to the group to which they were randomly assigned, regardless of whether they received the study medication.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was available for 95.6% of fetuses, and reported comparisons of those lost to follow-up did not suggest differential missingness between randomized groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was assessed for 95.6% of fetuses. ... The baseline characteristics of the women whose fetuses were lost to follow-up did not differ significantly between the two study groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome used prespecified standardized diagnostic criteria, certified clinical examiners, and blinded review for children requiring retrospective adjudication, within a double-blind trial.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: For 28 children who were not evaluated at 2 years of age but were not declared free of cerebral palsy at the age of 1 year, two pediatric neurologists who were unaware of the treatment assignment judged whether the children had moderate or severe cerebral palsy on the basis of a review of the 1-year examination.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered, the primary outcome and secondary cerebral-palsy analysis were explicitly prespecified, and the paper clearly distinguished nonprespecified subgroup and sensitivity analyses, providing little indication of selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Prespecified secondary outcomes included various maternal outcomes and complications; adverse events potentially attributable to the study intervention; neonatal complications; cerebral palsy at 2 years of age classified as mild, moderate, or severe; stillbirth; infant death; and scores on the Bayley Scales of Infant Development II.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns because allocation-sequence concealment was not explicitly described. All other domains were at low risk owing to double blinding, intention-to-treat analysis, high follow-up, standardized outcome assessment, and clear prespecification of outcomes and analyses.
